name: KalshiDash3 fee-aware ROI screen, v1
what_this_is: A deterministic screen that ranks a market by the modelled RETURN ON CAPITAL of crossing the spread right now, after fees. It is this project's model, not a Kalshi product. Two implementations read this one file: assets/live.js (browser, tick-level) and scripts/roi_scan.py (GitHub Actions, committed snapshot). scripts/tests/test_roi_parity.mjs asserts both produce the same numbers on the same fixture.
what_this_is_not: Not a price forecast and not advice. The model reads the current book, so its 'edge' is the difference between a blended quote and the price you must actually pay. If the book is already right, the edge is zero. Demo prices may not reflect real markets: https://docs.kalshi.com/getting_started/demo_env

swing_alert.rule: Alert when |last_price − last_price_at_previous_observation| >= threshold_dollars, in EITHER direction. Comparison is between consecutive observations of the same market ticker, never between a bid and an ask.
swing_alert.why: This is the threshold the project brief specified.
swing_alert.verified_against: no API field: this is a project rule, stated here so the number is not buried in code

inputs.note: Every input is a documented field of the public, unauthenticated demo API. No input is estimated from anything outside the API.

fields.name: depth_at_bid
fields.from: last element of orderbook_fp.yes_dollars [price_dollars, count_fp]; arrays are ascending, best bid last

fields.name: depth_at_ask
fields.from: last element of orderbook_fp.no_dollars: a NO bid at Y is a YES ask at 1-Y, so that count is the size a YES buyer can lift

fields.name: momentum_dollars
fields.from: last − last price N minutes ago, from this project's own observation series (browser ticks or data/live/price_history.json); candlesticks cannot supply it for a settled window shorter than 1 minute

parameters.weights_note: Fair estimate q = 0.45*mid + 0.35*microprice + 0.20*last, then a momentum tilt is added. The three weights sum to 1.0, so q stays inside the quoted range before the tilt. mid = (bid+ask)/2; microprice = (bid*ask_size + ask*bid_size)/(ask_size+bid_size), i.e. the side with more resting size pulls the estimate. 'microprice' is a standard order-book statistic defined here; it is not a Kalshi field.

trend.rule: tilt = weight * clip(momentum / reference_move, -1, 1). A 10c move in the lookback window shifts q by at most 2c.

parameters.filters_note: Hard gates, applied before ranking. max_entry_price keeps the screen out of the 95c-99c region where a cent of rounding dominates the answer. require_seed_category means only markets whose series ticker appears in the official fee schedule (https://kalshi.com/docs/kalshi-fee-schedule.pdf) can be picked; keyword-only topic matches are excluded from the picks feed and still appear in the all-events feed. price_levels_inside_zero_and_one: a side is priced only when its quoted level sits strictly between $0.00 and $1.00. GET /markets answers 0.0000 rather than omitting the field when a side has no resting order (measured: 127 of the 387 open in-scope markets in data/live/markets.json, collected 2026-11-20T15:19:53Z), and at a cost of exactly $0.00 the ratio (win − cost) / cost has no value — a division by zero in the scheduled scan, +Infinity in the browser, which would rank a pinned quote as the best edge on the board. Such a side is refused with a stated reason and the market falls to 'no buyable side'; it is never repriced. Pinned by cases zero-level-quote-reject and zero-ask-only-buy-no-side-reject of scripts/tests/fixtures_roi_parity.json (browser/CI parity) and by scripts/tests/test_roi_scan_snapshot.py (the real scan over the real snapshot).

fees.taker_formula: fee = round up (M_taker x 0.07 x C x P x (1 - P))
fees.maker_formula: fee = round up (M_maker x 0.0175 x C x P x (1 - P))
fees.round_up_definition: rounded up such that the fee + positionCost is rounded to a centicent; implemented here as rounding the total fee up to the next cent, which reproduces every row of the schedule's general table exactly (see scripts/tests/test_fees.py)
fees.settlement_fee: zero for simple yes/no determinations; may apply for sub-cent scalar settlement
fees.payout: YES holders receive $1 per contract on a yes outcome; NO holders receive $1 per contract on a no outcome

series_multipliers.note: Transcribed ONLY from the fee schedule's Non-Standard Fees table for series this project can put in scope. Absent series use the general default (taker 1, maker 0). The PDF does not publish a complete machine-readable list, so any series not listed here is treated as general and is flagged as such rather than guessed.

KXELECTIRAN.description_in_pdf: Will Iran hold a presidential election?

steps: 1. q = clip(w_mid*mid + w_micro*micro + w_last*last, 0, 1) + trend tilt, then clipped to [0.01, 0.99].
2. YES entry: pay the ask. unit_fee_yes = M_taker*0.07*ask*(1-ask). cost_yes = ask + unit_fee_yes. ev_yes = q - cost_yes. roi_yes = ev_yes / cost_yes.

3. NO entry: pay (1 - bid) for a NO contract whose price is P_no = 1 - bid. unit_fee_no = M_taker*0.07*P_no*(1-P_no). cost_no = P_no + unit_fee_no. ev_no = (1 - q) - cost_no. roi_no = ev_no / cost_no.

4. side = whichever of roi_yes / roi_no is larger; score = that roi. A pick therefore means: after paying the spread and the documented taker fee, the modelled payout still exceeds the cost by this fraction of the cost.
5. Drop the market if any hard filter fails. Rank by score desc, keep top_k.
scoring.why_roi_not_edge: The brief asks for 'high ROI', so the ranking quantity is return-on-capital (profit / capital at risk), not raw cents of edge. A 3c edge on a 6c contract is a bigger ROI than a 6c edge on a 90c contract; near the extremes the capital at risk is small but so is the probability, which is why the hit-rate measurement below is published next to the score.

validation.method: Out-of-sample replay on markets that have already settled, using only information available before close. For each settled market the collector fetches 1-minute candlesticks covering the 120 minutes before close_time, forms the signal from that candle's yes_bid/yes_ask/price close only, and scores it with the same parameters. The entry price is the candle's best ask (buy YES) or 1 - best bid (buy NO). The bet settles at $1 for the winning side and $0 for the losing side, per the settlement doc.
honest_limits: The replay cannot see the order-book depth or the momentum at signal time (candlesticks carry price aggregates only), so the validation runs a REDUCED feature set: mid and last only, micro weight reallocated to mid. The live score is therefore not identical to the validated score, and the page says so.

Only markets still inside the live window are readable: settled markets and their candlesticks move to GET /historical/* once the cutoff advances (https://docs.kalshi.com/getting_started/historical_data).
Sample is whatever the demo exchange happens to have settled; it is small and it is demo data. A measured hit rate is not a promise about real markets.
The result field is used exactly as returned: yes, no or scalar. Scalar settlements are excluded from a yes/no hit-rate claim rather than coerced into one.

catalyst_links.rule: For a >=10c move, the site may show links ONLY if a URL appears literally in that market's own official text fields (rules_primary, rules_secondary, subtitle, yes_sub_title, no_sub_title) as returned by GET /markets, or the market/event record link. The GET /markets response schema has no news field.
catalyst_links.label_shown: source this market settles on (from its own rules text)
catalyst_links.never_shown: any claim that a given article caused the move
catalyst_links.empty_case: no URL in the official record -> the cell is left blank and labelled 'no source URL in the market record', never filled by guesswork
